content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: overtime for 14 payments agents plus delayed breaks and cancelled general coaching lifts service level to 80.4% for 14:30-16:30, at ₹2,895.","why":"The payments surge is driven by the open card authorisation gateway incident (INC-20261001-6607). Card_declined calls account for about 300 of the roughly 400 extra calls. With no action, the window is predicted at 62.0% (payments 56.4%) with 8.5% abandons. P3 is the only plan that meets the 80% target at the lowest cost: it predicts 80.4% overall, payments 77.7%, general 86.7%, and 4.6% abandons. Rest of day improves to 86.8%. It follows policy.","trade_offs":["P1 costs nothing but only reaches 69.9% (payments 64.2%) with 6.5% abandons, well short of target.","P2 (outage message, chat deflection, callback) costs ₹144 but reaches only 64.6%. Its levers start late (15:45), so they do little within the window.","P4 adds the outage levers to P3 for ₹3,039 and lands at 80.0% (payments 77.1%), no better than P3 for ₹144 more.","General is not put at risk: it rises to 86.7% under P3 despite delayed breaks and cancelled coaching, because its dip looks like overflow from payments rather than a separate cause."],"watch":"Payments stays below 80% on its own (77.7%) even though the overall target is met. Track how many of the 14 agents accept overtime, since a shortfall puts the target at risk. Also watch the incident status: if the gateway outage runs past 16:30 or card_declined volume keeps climbing, reassess and consider the outage IVR message."}
